# Corruption (INEGI ENCIG)

I am turning INEGI **ENCIG** (Encuesta Nacional de Calidad e Impacto Gubernamental) state rates into a corruption pressure.

ENCIG asks adults (18+) in cities of 100,000+ about contact with government and whether corruption happened during trámites, payments, or service requests. Higher victimization = higher pressure (**1 = most pressure**).

**Pros:** official state estimates every two years (2013-2025); designed for national and state inference.  
**Cons:** urban sample only (cities 100k+); state level only (no full municipal coverage); biennial, not annual.

We decided that for now, assessing this pressure at the state level is fine (same decision as labor poverty). So I use the six GoC states: Baja California, Baja California Sur, Sonora, Sinaloa, Jalisco, and Nayarit.

I downloaded two interactive tabular series from INEGI:

1. **Prevalence** (victims per 100,000 people who contacted government): share of people who were victims at least once. I clean and plot it for comparison.  
2. **Incidence** (corruption acts per 100,000): counts acts, so one person can contribute more than once. **This is the locked pressure.** We chose incidence because each corrupt trámite is a separate negative hit; intensity should show up in the score even when the same people are affected over and over again. Prevalence only asks whether someone was hit at least once, so it underweights places where victims face repeated acts.

---

**To download:**

- Go to <https://en.www.inegi.org.mx/programas/encig/2025/#tabular_data>.
- Click on "Tabular data" and click on "Corruption prevalence rate per 100 000 inhabitants by state and year" and "Corruption incidence rate per hundred thousand inhabitants by state and year"
- For each of these, select all years, states, and variables.  
- Hit "Consultar" and download the results to bring into Mazu at `/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/_raw_data/inegi_corruption_ENCIG/d2026`

---

*Outline of the script:*

1. Explore both Excel downloads (prevalence and incidence).  
2. Read CONAPO population for year-specific weights (needed when Region_9 spans two states).  
3. Clean both rates into tidy state × year tables for the GoC.  
4. Compare three ways to rescale incidence from 0-1; use Option B again (rate / 100,000).  
5. Map Option B onto GoC `rgn_id`s and save.  
6. Explore with `plotly`.

---

```{r constants}
quantile_p <- 0.90

# absolute ceiling for Option B: rate is "per 100,000 inhabitants"
rate_per <- 100000

goc_states <- c(
  "Baja California",
  "Baja California Sur",
  "Sonora",
  "Sinaloa",
  "Jalisco",
  "Nayarit"
)
```

### What the two rates mean (from INEGI notes)

| Series | Numerator | Denominator | × |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Prevalence** | people 18+ who did at least one trámite / payment / service request (or in-person contact with a public servant) **and** were victims of corruption in some trámite | people 18+ who did at least one such contact | 100,000 |
| **Incidence** | number of trámites / payments / service requests **where** a corruption act happened | same contact population | 100,000 |

So prevalence is closer to knowing how many individuals were victims. Incidence can be larger because one person can have several corrupt trámites. We lock incidence so that repeated hits still raise the pressure.

## 1. CONAPO state population (year-specific weights)

Same as in the labor poverty script: sum `POB_TOTAL` so each GoC state-year has one population weight. I need this when Region_9 inherits both Jalisco and Nayarit.

```{r conapo-read}
conapo_raw <- read_csv(conapo_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r conapo-aggregate}
state_population <- conapo_raw %>%
  select(CLAVE_ENT, NOM_ENT, ANO, SEXO, POB_TOTAL) %>%
  filter(NOM_ENT %in% goc_states) %>%
  group_by(year = ANO, estado = NOM_ENT) %>%
  summarize(poblacion = sum(POB_TOTAL, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r conapo-check}
state_population %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2013, 2017, 2021, 2025)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = poblacion) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "CONAPO projected total population (GoC states; selected ENCIG years)",
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )

stopifnot(all(goc_states %in% unique(state_population$estado)))
```

## 2. Clean prevalence and incidence

I skip the title block, keep the point estimate, and drop the national aggregate row when I want GoC-only series. I also keep an all-Mexico state series for Option C later.

```{r read-encig-fun}
# shared tidy reader for both ENCIG tabular downloads
read_encig_rate <- function(path, rate_name) {
  raw <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Tabulado", col_names = FALSE)

  # row 7 in excel (1-indexed) is the header; data start after that
  dat <- raw %>%
    slice(8:n()) %>%
    setNames(c(
      "year", "estado", "rate", "cv", "se", "ci_low", "ci_high"
    )) %>%
    mutate(
      year = suppressWarnings(as.integer(year)),
      estado = str_trim(as.character(estado)),
      rate = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(rate)),
      cv = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(cv)),
      se = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(se)),
      ci_low = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ci_low)),
      ci_high = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ci_high)),
      series = rate_name
    ) %>%
    # footnotes / blank rows have non-numeric year
    filter(!is.na(year), !is.na(estado), estado != "") %>%
    select(series, year, estado, rate, cv, se, ci_low, ci_high)

  dat
}
```

```{r clean-both}
encig_prev_all <- read_encig_rate(prev_path, "prevalence")
encig_inc_all <- read_encig_rate(inc_path, "incidence")

encig_all <- bind_rows(encig_prev_all, encig_inc_all)

encig_mexico <- encig_all %>%
  filter(!str_detect(estado, regex("Estados Unidos Mexicanos", ignore_case = TRUE)))

encig_goc <- encig_mexico %>%
  filter(estado %in% goc_states)

encig_national <- encig_all %>%
  filter(str_detect(estado, regex("Estados Unidos Mexicanos", ignore_case = TRUE)))
```

```{r clean-checks}
encig_goc %>%
  count(series, year) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = n) %>%
  kable(caption = "GoC state rows per ENCIG year (expect 6)")

encig_goc %>%
  group_by(series) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(rate)),
    min_rate = min(rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate = max(rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "GoC ENCIG rate summary")

encig_goc %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  select(series, estado, rate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = rate) %>%
  arrange(desc(incidence)) %>%
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "2025 GoC prevalence vs incidence (per 100,000)")

# |estado              | prevalence| incidence|
# |:-------------------|----------:|---------:|
# |Sonora              |    18355.5|   36864.5|
# |Sinaloa             |    19836.3|   31994.7|
# |Baja California     |    15598.5|   23879.7|
# |Baja California Sur |    11575.0|   23381.7|
# |Jalisco             |    13514.0|   18306.3|
# |Nayarit             |     8914.8|   17663.5|
```

## 3. Rescale incidence to corruption pressure 0-1

Higher incidence = higher pressure. Before locking one rescale, I compare three options (same idea as labor poverty):

| Option | Formula | What pressure = 1 means |
|---|---|---|
| A. GoC 90th | `(rate - GoC min) / (GoC p90 - GoC min)`, clipped | among the worst GoC state-years |
| B. Absolute /100,000 | `rate / 100000` | 100,000 corrupt acts per 100,000 people who contacted government |
| C. Mexico 90th | `(rate - MX min) / (MX p90 - MX min)`, clipped | as bad as the national high end |

Option B is the natural absolute scale: an incidence of 36,865 per 100,000 becomes pressure 0.369.

```{r incidence-refs}
inc_goc <- encig_goc %>%
  filter(series == "incidence", !is.na(rate))

inc_mx <- encig_mexico %>%
  filter(series == "incidence", !is.na(rate))

ref_goc_low <- min(inc_goc$rate)
ref_goc_high <- as.numeric(quantile(inc_goc$rate, probs = quantile_p))

ref_mx_low <- min(inc_mx$rate)
ref_mx_high <- as.numeric(quantile(inc_mx$rate, probs = quantile_p))

stopifnot(ref_goc_high > ref_goc_low, ref_mx_high > ref_mx_low)

tibble(
  option = c("A. GoC 90th", "B. Absolute /100,000", "C. Mexico 90th"),
  ref_low = c(ref_goc_low, 0, ref_mx_low),
  ref_high = c(ref_goc_high, rate_per, ref_mx_high),
  n_obs_in_ref = c(nrow(inc_goc), NA_integer_, nrow(inc_mx))
) %>%
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "Reference anchors for the three incidence rescales")
```

```{r incidence-scale-three}
inc_compare <- inc_goc %>%
  mutate(
    pressure_goc90 = (rate - ref_goc_low) / (ref_goc_high - ref_goc_low),
    pressure_goc90 = pmin(pmax(pressure_goc90, 0), 1),
    pressure_abs = rate / rate_per,
    pressure_abs = pmin(pmax(pressure_abs, 0), 1),
    pressure_mx90 = (rate - ref_mx_low) / (ref_mx_high - ref_mx_low),
    pressure_mx90 = pmin(pmax(pressure_mx90, 0), 1)
  )
```

```{r incidence-compare-2025}
inc_compare %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  select(
    estado, rate,
    pressure_goc90, pressure_abs, pressure_mx90
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(rate)) %>%
  kable(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "2025 GoC corruption incidence: raw rate and pressure under three rescales"
  )

# |estado              |     rate| pressure_goc90| pressure_abs| pressure_mx90|
# |:-------------------|--------:|--------------:|------------:|-------------:|
# |Sonora              | 36864.54|          1.000|        0.369|         1.000|
# |Sinaloa             | 31994.67|          0.848|        0.320|         0.843|
# |Baja California     | 23879.71|          0.558|        0.239|         0.555|
# |Baja California Sur | 23381.67|          0.541|        0.234|         0.537|
# |Jalisco             | 18306.35|          0.360|        0.183|         0.357|
# |Nayarit             | 17663.53|          0.337|        0.177|         0.335|
```

```{r incidence-compare-timeseries}
inc_compare_ts <- inc_compare %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    pressure_goc90 = mean(pressure_goc90),
    pressure_abs = mean(pressure_abs),
    pressure_mx90 = mean(pressure_mx90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pressure_"),
    names_to = "rescale",
    values_to = "pressure"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rescale = recode(
      rescale,
      pressure_goc90 = "A. GoC 90th",
      pressure_abs = "B. Absolute value out of 100,000",
      pressure_mx90 = "C. Mexico 90th"
    )
  )

plot_compare_ts <- plot_ly(
  inc_compare_ts,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~pressure,
  color = ~rescale,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "GoC mean corruption incidence pressure over time: three rescaling options (notice A and C are the same)",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Mean pressure (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05))
  )

plot_compare_ts
```

I am using **Option B** for now (`pressure = incidence_rate / 100000`). Same spirit as labor poverty Option B: easy to explain, and easy to swap later.

```{r save-option-b}
# Option B: absolute incidence share (acts per person who contacted government)
inc_scaled <- inc_compare %>%
  transmute(
    year, estado,
    incidence_rate = rate,
    pressure = pressure_abs
  )

inc_scaled %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  arrange(desc(pressure)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Locked Option B: 2025 incidence pressure by state")
```

### Prevalence under the same absolute rescale (comparison)

Prevalence stays as a check: it answers "how many people were hit at least once," while incidence answers "how many acts happened."

```{r prevalence-option-b}
prev_scaled <- encig_goc %>%
  filter(series == "prevalence", !is.na(rate)) %>%
  transmute(
    year, estado,
    prevalence_rate = rate,
    pressure_prevalence = pmin(pmax(rate / rate_per, 0), 1)
  )

prev_scaled %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  arrange(desc(pressure_prevalence)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Comparison: 2025 prevalence as rate per 100,000 by state")
```

## 4. Map Option B incidence onto `rgn_id` and save

State incidence values are inherited by every GoC `rgn_id` in that state (`municipality_to_rgnid_update.csv`). Region_9 spans Jalisco and Nayarit, so I take a CONAPO population-weighted mean of the two state pressures.

```{r mun-rgn-lookup}
mun_lookup <- read_csv(mun_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    estado = str_trim(estado),
    rgn_id = as.character(rgn_id)
  )

estado_to_rgn <- mun_lookup %>%
  distinct(estado, rgn_id) %>%
  mutate(estado_key = str_to_upper(estado)) %>%
  select(estado_key, rgn_id)

estado_to_rgn %>%
  arrange(rgn_id, estado_key) %>%
  kable(caption = "Estado to rgn_id (unique pairs from municipality lookup)")
```

```{r option-b-to-rgn}
inc_rgn <- inc_scaled %>%
  mutate(estado_key = str_to_upper(estado)) %>%
  left_join(estado_to_rgn, by = "estado_key", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(state_population, by = c("year", "estado")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rgn_id), !is.na(pressure))

corruption_encig_pressure <- inc_rgn %>%
  group_by(rgn_id, year) %>%
  summarise(
    pressure = if (n() == 1 || all(is.na(poblacion))) {
      mean(pressure)
    } else {
      weighted.mean(pressure, w = poblacion, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    n_states = n_distinct(estado),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rgn_num = as.integer(str_remove(rgn_id, "Region_")),
    pressure = round(pressure, 4)
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, rgn_num) %>%
  select(rgn_id, year, pressure)

corruption_encig_pressure %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Option B corruption incidence pressure by rgn_id (2025)")
```

```{r save-option-b}
write_csv(corruption_encig_pressure, here::here(output_dir, "corruption_encig_pressure.csv"))
write_csv(corruption_encig_pressure, here::here("_pressures/social/output", "corruption_encig_pressure.csv"))
```


## 5. Explore with plotly

### Incidence pressure by state (Option B)

```{r plot-incidence}
plot_inc <- plot_ly(
  inc_scaled,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~pressure,
  color = ~estado,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers",
  text = ~paste0(
    estado, "<br>", year,
    "<br>incidence per 100k: ", round(incidence_rate, 0),
    "<br>pressure: ", round(pressure, 3)
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Corruption incidence pressure (ENCIG, Option B), for the GoC states",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Pressure (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Estado"))
  )

plot_inc
```

### Incidence vs prevalence (absolute /100,000)

```{r plot-inc-vs-prev}
both_long <- bind_rows(
  inc_scaled %>%
    transmute(year, estado, series = "incidence", pressure),
  prev_scaled %>%
    transmute(year, estado, series = "prevalence", pressure = pressure_prevalence)
)

# goC mean of each series over time
both_ts <- both_long %>%
  group_by(year, series) %>%
  summarise(pressure = mean(pressure), .groups = "drop")

plot_both <- plot_ly(
  both_ts,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~pressure,
  color = ~series,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "GoC mean: incidence vs prevalence (both as rate/100,000)",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Mean pressure (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05))
  )

plot_both
```

### Regional pressure time series 

```{r plot-rgn}
rgn_labels <- c(
  "Region_1" = "Western Upper Gulf",
  "Region_2" = "Western Midriff Islands",
  "Region_3" = "Western Central Gulf",
  "Region_4" = "Western Southern Gulf",
  "Region_5" = "Eastern Upper Gulf",
  "Region_6" = "Eastern Midriff Islands",
  "Region_7" = "Southern Sonora Coast",
  "Region_8" = "Sinaloa Coast",
  "Region_9" = "Southeastern Gulf"
)

rgn_colors <- c(
  "Region_1" = "#C03729",
  "Region_2" = "#E68C7C",
  "Region_3" = "#FC8F24",
  "Region_4" = "#dcaa38",
  "Region_5" = "#cbd2a0",
  "Region_6" = "#98a25a",
  "Region_7" = "#747428",
  "Region_8" = "#627391",
  "Region_9" = "#8d61a9"
)

plot_rgn <- corruption_encig_pressure %>%
  mutate(
    region = recode(rgn_id, !!!rgn_labels),
    region = factor(region, levels = unname(rgn_labels))
  ) %>%
  plot_ly(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~pressure,
    color = ~region,
    colors = setNames(unname(rgn_colors), unname(rgn_labels)),
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines+markers"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Corruption incidence pressure by GoC region (Option B)",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Pressure (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Region"))
  )

plot_rgn
```

## Next steps

1. Re-knit on Mazu once the xlsx files live under `_raw_data/inegi_corruption_ENCIG/d2026`.  
2. Optionally swap Option B for A or C if the absolute scale feels too muted next to other social pressures.  
3. CNGMD municipal anti-corruption tables remain a separate track (administrative capacity / reporting), not a substitute for ENCIG victimization.
